summary: Kickoff for Delta Grove pilot and onboarding. Covered deployment modes (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC), security requirements (KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs), initial perf goals, and next steps for a two-week benchmarking pilot. Customer expressed production concerns around latency for routing/dispatch workloads and data residency. Agreed pilot scope and documentation to exchange.
questions: What quantization / model variants do you recommend for low-latency inference?
How do rollouts and fallbacks work across Dedicated and Hosted?
What telemetry do we get for token-level cost breakdowns?
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-29
Time: 15:00 - 15:52 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Avery Cole (Redwood AE), Sanju Patel (Redwood CSM), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Markus Flynn (Delta Grove - Head of ML), Rita Huang (Delta Grove - Platform Eng), Samir Patel (Delta Grove - Security), Elena Ruiz (Delta Grove - PM)

Auto-summary: Quick intro, secure deployment questions, agree pilot scope for two-week benchmark, handoffs for security docs and sandbox endpoints.

00:00 Avery (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Avery from Redwood inference, I'm with Sanju and Lena from our onboarding team.
00:08 Markus (Delta Grove): Thanks, hi uh Markus here. Appreciate the time. Quick note we got lots to cover about vpc and perf.
00:15 Sanju (Redwood): We'll do a run through scope, security, then the perf plan and next steps.
00:22 Rita (Delta Grove): I'm mostly interested in how the private deployment will look w network peering and egress controls.
00:30 Lena (Redwood): Right, we'll show a few options. Briefly: Hosted API is fastest to spin up, Dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput, and Private gives you VPC/on-prem with full network control.
00:46 Samir (Delta Grove): For us security is primary—SOC2 a must, and we need KMS/HSM support, plus audit logs retained for a year.
00:56 Avery (Redwood): Yep we have SOC2 documents and optional KMS integration patterns. HSM-backed KMS is supported through partner integrations; we'll share specifics.
01:09 Elena (Delta Grove): Timeline—we want to start pilot in mid-November and go prod in Jan if results look good.
01:16 Avery (Redwood): Sounds doable, pilot is usually 2 weeks of benchmarking and model tuning.

04:02 Lena (Redwood): For the latency sensitive path — you mentioned routing/dispatch — we often recommend Dedicated or Private with smaller quantized models and batching set to low-latency configs. Also prefix KV caching for repeated context.
04:29 Markus (Delta Grove): How impactful is quantization on quality? We can't lose the NLU fidelity on our routing models.
04:36 Lena (Redwood): There's a trade-off, 4-bit or int8 can shave quite a bit off latency and cost, but we usually run quality checks against your eval set. Redwood Optimize will flag regressions.
04:50 Rita (Delta Grove): We use proprietary data in prompts; does Redwood retain logs? What's the default retention?
04:58 Sanju (Redwood): By default hosted logs are retained 30 days, audit logs are longer for enterprise customers; for Private you control retention and we can disable retention on request. We'll include the retention matrix in the pack.

08:12 Samir (Delta Grove): Network — we need to peer via a single transit VPC, with strict egress rules. Also IP allowlists and private endpoints.
08:22 Lena (Redwood): Under Private deployment we provide a customer-managed control plane pattern, VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink are common. We'll draw the diagram for you.

11:00 Markus (Delta Grove): Metrics — what telemetry do we get? We need token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency percentiles.
11:10 Avery (Redwood): Console provides token-level cost, per-model and per-route latency p50/p95/p99, tracing hooks and error analysis. We can turn on additional debug tracing during the pilot.

14:40 Rita (Delta Grove): Are there any concurrency limits or autoscaling quirks to be aware of with Dedicated?
14:48 Lena (Redwood): Dedicated is a reserved GPU pool; autoscaling policies are configurable, and we support burst capacity. Quirks: warmup for KV cache matters for cold starts but steady-state throughput is predictable.

18:05 Markus (Delta Grove): Competitors — we've looked at Anthropic and TritonServe internally, what would be the main differentiators you'd highlight?
18:13 Avery (Redwood): Focus is production levers: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, built-in rollouts and fallbacks, and tooling for cost vs latency tradeoffs — Redwood Optimize recommends batching/quantization profiles for your workload.

21:59 Elena (Delta Grove): Pilot acceptance criteria — we propose: 1) p95 latency under 250ms for 95% of calls in a representative window, 2) no regression >2% on intent classification accuracy, 3) operational runbook produced.
22:15 Avery (Redwood): Fine, we'll run the perf tests and validate against your eval set.

25:40 Sanju (Redwood): Security handoff — we'll attach SOC2, network diagram, SAML SSO setup, and KMS patterns to the shared folder. Also SSO SAML and RBAC mapping examples.
25:56 Samir (Delta Grove): For KMS we want HSM; can you confirm vendor integrations?
26:05 Sanju (Redwood): Yes, we have patterns for AWS CloudHSM via custom KMS or using your organization KMS with envelope encryption; details in the security doc.

30:12 Lena (Redwood): On the bench plan: we'll provision sandbox endpoints in your VPC (or Redwood-hosted sandbox if you prefer), run a 1-hour cold start test, then a 4-hour steady-state QPS ramp with your workload. We'll capture token counts, p50/p95/p99, and cost-per-token.
30:33 Markus (Delta Grove): We'll provide a 24-hour sample trace and evaluation prompts; also our expected QPS for the busiest route is ~120 QPS.
30:42 Lena (Redwood): Noted. For 120 QPS we may suggest Dedicated with auto-burst unless latency constraints force Private. We'll model cost tradeoffs as part of pilot.

34:10 Rita (Delta Grove): Any required changes to our infra for Private? Networking aside, we run on-prem data classification services.
34:18 Avery (Redwood): Private has an option to run the control plane inside your VPC and optionally an on-prem runtime; we'll need a small inbound port list and service account. We'll provide a runbook.

37:55 Samir (Delta Grove): Audit logs — can we ship logs to our SIEM and control retention?
38:03 Sanju (Redwood): Yes SIEM shipping via syslog/S3 logging is supported for enterprise customers; retention fully configurable in Private.

41:00 Elena (Delta Grove): SOW — what does the pilot SOW typically include?
41:08 Avery (Redwood): Pilot SOW includes sandbox provisioning, two-week benchmark window, success criteria validation, a brief model tuning pass, and a follow-up report with recommendations and estimated cost to run in prod.

44:20 Rita (Delta Grove): Any gotchas — we've heard about KV cache invalidation leading to perf blips.
44:28 Lena (Redwood): Yeah, cache invalidation can cause spikes on rollouts; we recommend staged rollouts and warmups. Our rollout tooling supports canary + auto-fallback to a stable variant.

47:50 Markus (Delta Grove): Ok recap — pilot mid-Nov, 2 weeks, provide QPS/data, Redwood sends security pack and pricing, and Lena sets up sandbox endpoints.
47:58 Avery (Redwood): Correct. We'll also do a 2-hour deep perf run with your team during benchmarking week.
48:08 Sanju (Redwood): I'll put the security docs in the shared folder right after this call.
48:15 Mark(us) (Delta Grove): (brief chuckle) Sorry Markus? Yes, thanks.
48:20 Elena (Delta Grove): Next meeting — schedule a planning call the week before pilot start to align test dataset and runbook.

50:55 Avery (Redwood): Thanks all. Any last questions?
51:02 Samir (Delta Grove): Can you include a simple diagram of our proposed Private topology?
51:08 Lena (Redwood): Yes, we'll attach a diagram and a sample CloudFormation/Terraform snippet for Private peering.
51:20 Avery (Redwood): Great. We'll follow up with all artifacts and a calendar invite for the perf window.
51:30 Meeting end.

References/links shared: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2.pdf, https://drive.example.com/delta-grove/pilot-pricing.xlsx, https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/private-vpc-diagram.png

Notes about transcript quality: auto-transcript had a few mis-attributions, some product names like "KV cache" transcribed as "K V cash" in places; speaker overlaps noted.
